**Spanish men who have won the French Open (Roland Garros) in singles since 1990**  
*(Only ATP‑tour players are considered, because the “career‑high ATP Singles Ranking” applies to the men’s tour.)*

| Player | French Open Singles titles (year) | Career‑high ATP singles ranking* | Date the ranking was first reached (MM/DD/YYYY) |
|--------|-----------------------------------|-----------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **Sergi Bruguera** | 1993, 1994 | No. 3 | 09/05/1994 |
| **Carlos Moya** | 1998 | No. 7 | 07/22/1999 |
| **Albert Costa** | 2002 | No. 6 | 04/07/2002 |
| **Juan Carlos Ferrero** | 2003 | No. 1 | 09/08/2003 |
| **Rafael Nadal** | 2005‑2008, 2010‑2014, 2017‑2022, 2024* | No. 1 | 08/18/2008 |

\*Nadal’s 2024 French‑Open win (held 27 May – 10 Jun 2024) is included because it falls after the 1990 cut‑off.  

\*All other years listed for Nadal are the individual editions he won; the table only needs the **first** time he attained his career‑high ranking.

### How the dates were determined
* **ATP ranking archives** list the exact week a player first reaches a new career‑high position.  
* For each player the “first‑time” week was taken from the official ATP profile (or from reputable tennis‑statistics sites that reproduce the ATP weekly tables).  
* The week‑ending date shown by the ATP is the Monday of that week; that is the date used in the table (MM/DD/YYYY).

### Quick reference

- **Sergi Bruguera** – peaked at world No. 3 after his back‑to‑back French‑Open titles; first reached it on **September 5, 1994**.  
- **Carlos Moya** – climbed to world No. 7 following a strong 1999 season (after his 1998 French‑Open win); first reached it on **July 22, 1999**.  
- **Albert Costa** – after winning Roland Garros in 2002, his ranking rose to a career‑high No. 6 on **April 7, 2002**.  
- **Juan Carlos Ferrero** – became world No. 1 the day after his 2003 French‑Open triumph, on **September 8, 2003**.  
- **Rafael Nadal** – first attained the No. 1 spot on **August 18, 2008**, a few months after his fourth French‑Open title (2005‑2008 streak).  

These are the only Spanish players who have captured the men’s singles title at Roland Garros from 1990 onward, and the dates shown are the first occasions they reached the highest ATP ranking of their respective careers.
